question: Neuron edits in the tower (hold / add at every position, constant strength) break when several are stacked. Do drug-like primitives stack better? (1) WHEN: apply only while the reply is written, optionally fading out (pharmacokinetics). (2) HOMEOSTASIS: rescale the residual stream after an edited floor back to the norm it would have had unedited. (3) RECEPTOR: shift a neuron's gate pre-activation (threshold) instead of writing its output, so the push scales with the neuron's own input. Separately, for suppression: does a soft ceiling c*tanh(a/c) or block-to-typical (mean) suppress an instructed feature with less damage than zeroing or a gain cut?
model: Qwen/Qwen3-4B bf16, chat template, enable_thinking=False, greedy, 80 new tokens (probes), 40 (capability).

part_A_stacking.finds: 7 harmless verified 4B single-neuron finds (neuron-landscape-4b / persona-cluster-4b), each at its board dose: alien L10N5045 -32, void L21N8400 -40, li-hui L16N6969 +32, semiconductor L10N6249 +40, cpp L8N1313 +40, lord L8N4434 +32, buddhist L11N6138 -40. Reframe (L13N614) excluded.
part_A_stacking.probes: 10 everyday/identity prompts (who are you, describe your morning, ...).
part_A_stacking.detector: per-find keyword regex (fixed below in pharm.py before the run); detection = fraction of the 10 replies matching.

primitives.add_all: a[n] += dose at every position (tower's current +x form; holds at this size behave the same since natural |a| << dose)
primitives.add_reply: a[n] += dose only at generated tokens (no prompt positions)
primitives.add_fade: as add_reply, times max(0, 1 - t/40), t = generated-token index
primitives.add_renorm: add_all, then the residual after each edited floor is rescaled per position to ||h - write|| (the norm it would have had unedited)
primitives.thresh: gate_proj pre-activation of n += delta at every position, delta > 0 calibrated per neuron so mean |change in a| on probe prompt tokens equals |dose|

part_A_stacking.stacks: K=1 (each find), K=2 (3 fixed subsets), K=4 (2 fixed subsets), K=7 (all), every primitive. Null: K=7 random neurons at the same floors and doses under add_all, add_fade, add_renorm.
part_A_stacking.metrics: SURVIVAL = mean detection of the stacked finds divided by mean of their own K=1 add_all detection; CAPABILITY = 16 factual QA with the edit on; REP4; NLL of the reply under the unedited model; NORM = ||h|| at floors 27 and 35 on reply tokens, edited / unedited.

part_B_suppression.features: sadness (system 'Respond in a sad, melancholic tone.') and formality (system 'Respond in a very formal, polished register.'), neutral contrast system as in steer-ladder-egret.
part_B_suppression.neurons: top-k positive-t neurons (feature reply minus contrast reply, MLP activation averaged over reply tokens teacher-forced after the plain prompt, 40 training prompts), floors 6-30, k in {16, 64, 256}.
part_B_suppression.primitives: zero (a=0), mean (a = contrast mean), gain (a*0.3), ceil (a = c*tanh(a/c), c = contrast 95th percentile of |a|). Null: k random neurons on the same floors under zero and ceil.
part_B_suppression.metrics: on 20 held-out prompts with the feature system prompt: SUPPRESSION = (instructed judge - edited judge) / (instructed judge - uninstructed judge), judge = unedited model 'Is this reply <sad|formal>?' logit Yes-No; CAPABILITY 16 QA (no system prompt, edit on); NLL of the reply under the unedited model with the same system prompt; REP4.

H1: Stacking hurts add_all: at K=7, add_all capability <= 12/16 OR survival < 0.6.
H2: add_reply or add_fade beats add_all at K=7: capability higher by >= 3 with survival >= 0.6.
H3: add_renorm beats add_all at K=7: capability higher by >= 3 with survival >= 0.6, and its NORM ratio is within 1.0 +/- 0.1.
H4: thresh keeps capability >= 14/16 at K=7 and survival >= 0.4 (context-dependent push still expresses).
H5: For suppression, at the k where ceil first reaches >= 0.5 suppression, ceil's capability >= zero's at the same k, for both features.
H6: Suppression beats random neurons: for the best primitive at k=64, suppression exceeds the random-neuron null by >= 0.3.
notes: Harmless features only. Outputs gitignored. Results feed new tower grammar only for primitives that pass; trained pills are a separate step (pills.py).

part_C_amendment.written: 2026-10-20, after part A had started (12 add_all/add_reply configs seen: single board-dose finds already cost capability), before any part C run
part_C_amendment.C1_attention_flattening: 'psychedelic' arm: divide every attention logit on a band of floors by T (scale q after q_norm by 1/T). Bands early 2-9, mid 10-21, late 22-33, all 0-35; T in {1.5, 3}; plus sharpening T=0.67 on mid. Probes = the 10 part-A prompts. Metrics: judge 'unusual, dreamlike or surreal' (logit Yes-No) minus base, distinct-2, rep4, NLL under the unedited model, capability 16 QA.
part_C_amendment.C2_feedback_dosing: set-point dose: before floor L, read p = residual projected on the find's write direction u = W_down[:,n]/|W_down[:,n]| (signed by the dose); add amount = clamp((target - p)/|W_down[:,n]|, 0, |dose|) with target = median p on unedited probe tokens + 0.5*|dose|*|W_down[:,n]|. Tops the concept up to a set point instead of a constant write. Stacks: void, cpp, all 7.
part_C_amendment.C3_combos_and_dose: add_fade+renorm at K=7; half board dose (0.5x) at K=7 under add_all, add_reply, add_fade, add_renorm.
part_C_amendment.H7: At least one attention-flattening setting raises the dreamlike judge by >= 3 with capability >= 14/16.
part_C_amendment.H8: Set-point dosing at K=7 keeps capability >= 3 higher than add_all at K=7 with stacked detection >= 0.3.
part_C_amendment.H9: At half dose, K=7: add_renorm or add_fade keeps capability >= 3 higher than add_all with stacked detection >= 0.3.

part_D_amendment.written: 2026-10-20, after part C; C2 set-point was open-loop (it read the residual at the edited floor's INPUT, so within a token it never saw its own write, and the clamp saturated) - H8 is re-marked UNTESTED, not failed
part_D_amendment.D_closed_loop: One-token-lag feedback. For each find (floor L, unit write direction u, sign s), read p = s * (residual at the OUTPUT of floor min(L+4, 35) . u) at the last position of each forward. Calibrate per find on the 10 probes (30 decode tokens): p0 = median p unedited, p1 = median p under add_all at board dose. Target = p0 + 0.5*(p1 - p0). Prompt pass: full dose (as add_all). Each reply token: dose = |dose| * clamp((target - p_prev)/(target - p0), 0, 1), p_prev from the previous token. So it doses fully while the concept is absent and backs off as the concept builds.
part_D_amendment.runs: solo void, semi, alien, cpp; lord+buddhist; all 7 (board dose).
part_D_amendment.H8b: At K=7, closed-loop dosing keeps capability >= 3 higher than add_all (0/16) with stacked detection >= 0.3; and solo it keeps the find (det >= 0.5x add_all's) with capability >= add_all + 3 for at least 2 of the 4 solo finds.

part_E_amendment.written: 2026-10-20, after parts A-D, before any part E run
part_E_amendment.E1_dose_curves: each of the 7 finds at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25 x board dose, add_all vs add_reply. Detection = keyword regex AND a judge (unedited model: 'Does this reply <find description>? Yes/No', logit, minus the unedited baseline), so faint traces count. Capability 16 QA.
part_E_amendment.E2_pairs: all 21 pairs of the 7 finds under add_reply at board dose (and add_fade for pairs that show synergy). SYNERGY = a pair's judge score for either member exceeds that member's solo add_reply judge score by >= 3 logits AND the pair keeps capability >= 8.
part_E_amendment.H10: reply-only shifts the cliff: for >= 3 of 7 finds, the lowest dose reaching judge >= +3 under add_reply keeps capability >= 3 higher than add_all at ITS lowest such dose.
part_E_amendment.H11: lord+buddhist is not unique: >= 2 other pairs show SYNERGY under add_reply.

part_F_amendment.written: 2026-10-20, after part E (9 of 21 pairs met SYNERGY; samples show some are judge-gaming), before any part F run
part_F_amendment.F_random_partner: For each of the 9 part-E SYNERGY pairs (a,b) and each member x in the pair, replace the OTHER member by a random neuron at the same floor and dose (3 seeds), add_reply, board dose; score x's judge. Partner-specific gain = pair judge for x minus mean random-partner judge for x.
part_F_amendment.H11b: A part-E synergy is partner-specific when the pair's judge for the gaining member exceeds the max of its 3 random-partner judges by >= 3. H11 holds in substance if >= 2 pairs besides lord+buddhist are partner-specific.

part_G_amendment.written: 2026-10-21, after parts A-F on Qwen3-4B, before any 8B run (user: 'sometimes we find things only on larger models, at least 8B')
part_G_amendment.model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B bf16 on a RunPod A40, same hooks, probes, capability set and judge recipe (the 8B judges itself).
part_G_amendment.finds: finds_8b.json: 3 God neurons (replicated in persona-switch) + 7 @Sauers_ catalogue identities (unverified).
part_G_amendment.G0_verify: each find at board dose, add_all and add_reply. VERIFIED = judge >= +3 under add_all OR add_reply. Unverified finds are reported and dropped from G2/G3.
part_G_amendment.G1_dose: each verified find at 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25 x board dose, add_all vs add_reply (1.0 reused from G0).
part_G_amendment.G2_pairs: all pairs of verified finds under add_reply at board dose; for each member x, the partner replaced by a random neuron at the partner's floor and dose (2 seeds). PARTNER-SPECIFIC = pair judge for x exceeds the max of its 2 random-partner judges by >= 3 AND pair capability >= 8. Pairs of two God neurons are reported but not counted for H13 (same concept).
part_G_amendment.G3_stack: all verified finds at once (K=all): add_all, add_reply, add_fade(40); null = one random neuron per find at the same floor and dose, add_all and add_reply. Norm ratio at floors 27 and 35.
part_G_amendment.H12: reply-only shifts the cliff on 8B: for >= half of verified finds, at the lowest dose reaching judge >= +3 under add_reply, capability is >= 3 higher than add_all at its lowest such dose.
part_G_amendment.H13: pairs combine on 8B: >= 3 non-God-God pairs are PARTNER-SPECIFIC.
part_G_amendment.H14: stacking holds better on 8B: K=all add_reply keeps capability >= 8/16 with mean member judge >= +3 (4B: K=7 reply-only capability 1-2/16).
part_G_amendment.H15: the random-neuron K=all null under add_all costs as much capability as the finds' K=all add_all (within 3/16), as on 4B.
